items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Louis Kepp played guitar. We had a good band.

ctx.x: Why did your brother play? Violin. What's his first name? Willie. Willie. Willie Foster. Yeah. I had Eddie Atkins. First we had Eddie Atkins.

We had Duterte for a while. We had Eddie Atkins and Duterte. King Oliver. Uh-huh. King Oliver. Uh-huh. Piku. Uh-huh. Had a guy called Chris. I never know what Chris's last name. Blaine Drum. Myself. Louis Kepp played guitar. We had a good band. Did you have some kind of a uniform? Yeah.
Yeah. And a guy with a uniform?

items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: Every year, he is, I don't know if I, how you do it, but he send a Christmas card to me and tell me that, Mr. and Mrs. Foster.

ctx.x: No, he's still living. I saw him last year.

Yeah, where's he? In Chicago. Still in Chicago. I'll tell you why. Because I got a, I got a postal card from, uh, from, uh, George Christmas, you know? And, uh, and, but he's not here. John Foster? Yeah, Pops Foster, they call it sometimes. Yeah, Pops Foster. I got a, I got a card from him Christmas. Every year, he is, I don't know if I, how you do it, but he send a Christmas card to me and tell me that, Mr. and Mrs. Foster. Christmas call to me and tell me that Mr. and Mrs. Foster.

items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1957-08-04
items.q: George Foster used to play bass, Phil, in Hunts with Joe Oliver. Because when we got the uniforms, he was playing with Joe Oliver.

ctx.x: Yes, he played trowel. He played bass, so he's dead now, too.

Yeah, he's dead. Well, Herbert used to play violin. Never knew him. Well, Willie Foster used to play with me and Joe Oliver. He used to play violin. George Foster used to play bass, Phil, in Hunts with Joe Oliver. Because when we got the uniforms, he was playing with Joe Oliver. When I went and got Joe Oliver and Nora Dutra and all of us was together. That's why he was there with us, right across. Now, at a few close, they had old man Umpra, was playing a few close. That's on Franklin. Of course they call it…

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: And Louis Kepertner was playing, and Louis Kepertner and Dave, they had a little band down in town, but I didn't know nothing about it, see. The Magnolia band. So they asked me to play with them.

ctx.x: Yeah I knew that Roy had played a different instrument.

Roy played guitar, see. Roy was our trumpet player for a long time then. Roy got on trombone. And we played, we played little things. The biggest thing we played when we had our band was that they'd lose that to drive and the funk back it. And then I got acquainted with Louis Kepertner, Eddie Gauldin's brother, which is a trombone player, Johnny Gauldin, he played violin and a little hurry up trombone, we called it hurry up trombone, see. When he couldn't play he looked like he was in a hurry to make his notes.…
Permit. Had you played in any band or anything? Did you play in any band or up there in Assumption Barrett before you came down?
